ledger.note: 437 BCE: Pandukabhaya founds the Anuradhapura Kingdom. Infobox 'Established 437 BC, per the Mahavamsa ... founded by King Pandukabhaya'; the page elsewhere has Pandukabhaya make Anuradhapura his capital in 377 BC and Prince Vijaya take control of the island from 543 BC. The region is the island without Ruhuna, the reading of the later situation.

237 BCE: two South Indian horse dealers, Sena and Guththika, seize the throne and rule for 22 years. The page puts the overthrow in the reign of 'Suratissa (247-237 BC)' and gives no separate date, so the year is the end of his reign (237 - 22 = 215, when Asela follows). Same state, same colour. Reviewer (sa-02-a, 2026-10-19): year moved from -247 (the start of Suratissa's reign) to -237 and confidence lowered to 2, since the year is inferred from the reign span.

205 BCE: the Chola prince Elara takes Anuradhapura. Asela is 'overthrown by the Chola prince Elara (205-161 BC), who rules for 44 years'; the Dutthagamani page says 45 years; the Chola dynasty page has the Mahavamsa's Ellalan conquer Rajarata 'in 235 BCE'. A usurper of Chola origin, not the Chola state: no occupation is drawn.

region.text: Ruhuna, 'a small kingdom in south-east Sri Lanka outside of the influence of Rajarata in the north' (Hambantota, Monaragala, Matara and Ampara districts as the reading of 'the south')

ledger.note: 161 BCE: Dutthagamani unites the island. '161-137 BC: Dutthagamani defeats Elara at the battle at Vijithapura and unifies the whole country under one king'; he comes from Ruhuna ('Kavantissa's small kingdom in south-east Sri Lanka'), which joins the Anuradhapura throne. Year and place: the page's reign span and my reading of Ruhuna.

161 BCE: Elara falls and Dutthagamani becomes king at Anuradhapura. The page gives 'reigned from 161 BC to 137 BC', the climax 'at the eastern gate of Anuradhapura' and a four-month siege of Vijithapura; no year for the war itself.
103 BCE: five Dravidian chiefs invade and rule Anuradhapura until 89 BCE ('Five Dravidian chiefs invade and rule until 89 BC, when Valagamba (89-77 BC) defeats them').
89 BCE: Valagamba defeats the five Dravidian chiefs and reigns until 77 BCE.
66: Vasabha founds the Lambakarana dynasty. 'Vasabha of the Lambakarana clan seizes power, ending the Vijayan dynasty and starting the first Lambakarana dynasty, which lasts over three centuries.'

433: a second invasion places six South Indian rulers in control of Anuradhapura, until Dhatusena defeats Pithiya and 'regains power in 459'; the page also says Dhatusena 'founds the Moriya (Maurya) dynasty' in 455.
459: Dhatusena defeats Pithiya, regains power and founds the Moriya dynasty (the page dates the foundation 455 and the regained power 459).
473: Kashyapa I moves the capital to Sigiriya. 'Kashyapa I (473-491, or 477-495 in another passage) used Sigiriya as his capital.'
492: the court returns to Anuradhapura. The page does not say when; the year follows the end of Kashyapa's span (491 in the infobox, 495 in another passage).
684: Manavanna starts the second Lambakanna dynasty, 'which lasts until Mahinda V'.

region.text: the north: the Jaffna peninsula, the Vanni and the dry zone around Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa and Trincomalee (Rajarata), which Rajaraja I called Mummudi-sola-mandalam

ledger.note: c. 993: the Cholas conquer the north. 'Chola Emperor Rajaraja I invades and conquers the north, which he names Mummudi-sola-mandalam'; the Mahinda V page: 'In 993, he fled to Ruhuna, the southern part of the country, following a large scale mutiny by his army'. The extent of 'the north' is my reading (Jaffna, the Vanni and the dry zone to Polonnaruwa and Trincomalee). Reviewer (sa-02-a, 2026-10-19): confidence 2: the page says only 'the north'; the districts are a reading.

notes:
Group sa-02-a. Page budget: five pages (Anuradhapura Kingdom, Dutthagamani, Mahinda V, Chola invasion of Sri Lanka, Chola dynasty).

NOT SPLIT. The Cliopatria row (-291..1017, five identical shapes) is one state in the page: the Anuradhapura Kingdom, 'founded by King Pandukabhaya in 437 BC' to 1017 AD, ruled by a succession of dynasties (Vijayan, first Lambakarana, Moriya, second Lambakanna). Dynasty changes and foreign usurpations are `rename` events; no new slug is needed. The Polonnaruwa kingdom after 1055 is a different state (Cliopatria has no row for it between 1017 and Ceylon in 1236); it needs a dossier from another group.

START. The dossier starts in -437 (infobox) instead of -291 (Cliopatria). The page gives two dates, 437 BC (kingdom) and 377 BC (Anuradhapura capital); both are Mahavamsa chronology. The five Cliopatria shapes are identical, so the breaks at 78, 439, 617 and 1015 are not territorial; they roughly match 66 (Lambakarana), 455/459 (Moriya), 684 (second Lambakanna) and 993/1017 (Chola).

EXTENT. Three corrections to the island-wide shape: before -161 the island without Ruhuna (the page: Ruhuna 'outside of the influence of Rajarata'; Dutthagamani 'first uniting the whole island'); from 993 the south and hill country only (the north Chola). The region for 'the north' and Ruhuna are my readings by Sri Lankan district; the Hambantota, Monaragala, Matara and Ampara districts stand for Ruhuna, which the page calls 'the south'. The Mahavamsa's 32 Tamil rulers in the north are not placed.

PAGES DISAGREE. Elara: 205-161 BC, 44 years (Anuradhapura) or 45 years (Dutthagamani); conquered Rajarata 'in 235 BCE' (Chola dynasty page). Sena and Guththika: they overthrew Suratissa (247-237 BC) and ruled '22 years', so 237-215 BC (the reviewer moved the event from -247 to -237). Kashyapa I: 473-491 or 477-495. Dhatusena: Moriya dynasty 455, power regained 459. Mahinda V: fled in 993 (Mahinda page) while the capital is destroyed in 1017 (Anuradhapura page). Pandukabhaya: kingdom 437 BC, capital 377 BC.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS. 'ruhuna' (Kavantissa's and Dutthagamani's small kingdom, before -161; also the retreat of Mahinda V from 993) has no Cliopatria row. 'chola-empire' (850-1259 in Cliopatria) is another group's; it should carry the north of Sri Lanka from c. 993 (Cliopatria has the island only from 1018). The medieval 'Sri Lankan Chola occupations' belong to the additions batch.

NOT DONE. The Sena I / Pandya wars (833-862) and the raids of 935-938 are dated but moved no border on the page. Rulers are not listed: the page has no full list.
